content.title: Thunder vs. Lakers: Live updates, highlights for Tuesday's game
content.text: Updated April 7, 2026, 11:23 p.m. CTThe Oklahoma City Thunder travel on the road to face the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday. This will be the fourth matchup of the season between the two squads. OKC has won the first three with its latest victory on Apr. 2.The Thunder (62-16) continue to roll along. They made easy work of the Utah Jazz in a 146-111 win on Sunday. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had a quiet 20 points and seven assists. Chet Holmgren tallied 21 points, seven rebounds and four blocks.Meanwhile, the Lakers (50-28) have walked through a post-apocalyptic world. They fell to the Dallas Mavericks in a 134-128 loss on Sunday. LeBron James turned back the clock with 30 points and 15 assists, but that wasn't enough to avoid the upset.For live updates of the Thunder's game against the Lakers, please regularly check back to this post: End 3Q: Thunder 93, Lakers 62This one is about over. Gilgeous-Alexander has 25 points and eight assists. He shouldn't need to check in again for the rest of the way. The Lakers just don't have enough NBA talent on the floor right now. Half: Thunder 65, Lakers 47Well, that was the wakeup call the Thunder needed. They finished the first half on a 23-5 run to take control of this game. Gilgeous-Alexander has 15 points and six assists. Joe has 12 points. Meanwhile, the Lakers' outside shooting luck eventually ran out. Los Angeles is scrambling for points now. Let's see how the second half plays out for OKC and if it can keep its distance on the scoreboard. 2Q, 7:26 left: Thunder 42, Lakers 42Not the greatest second-unit offense by the Thunder. Allowed the Lakers to get back into it. Kennard goes to the cup for the difficult finish. OKC calls a timeout as the game is tied back it up. End 1Q: Thunder 34, Lakers 27Gilgeous-Alexander's costly mistakes go unpunished. After fouling Vanderbilt on a 3-point attempt, he missed all three free throws. Gilgeous-Alexander has 11 points and five assists. The Lakers are using some hot outside shooting to stay close so far. 1Q, 3:22 left: Thunder 24, Lakers 19Offense is coming easily for the Thunder, as expected. Gilgeous-Alexander has seven points and five assists. They call a timeout. On the other side, Timme already has 10 points. Starting lineups:The Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Lu Dort, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. The Lakers will start Luke Kennard, Jake LaRavia, Rui Hachimura, Drew Timme and Deandre Ayton.What channel is Thunder vs. Lakers game on today?
